authoringRecipe.textureMustBePerObject: layer('texture',…) applied to a MULTI-selection silently no-ops. Select each object individually. This was the cause of the untextured relic.
authoringRecipe.displaceScaleIsFrequency: feature span is roughly 1000/scale world units. An 8 m prop needs scale ~320, NOT ~26 (which gives 38 m features and leaves a smooth egg).
authoringRecipe.coneNeedsBothCornerRadii: Cone spawns with cornerRadius 8 on BOTH ends; zeroing only cornerRadiusBottom leaves a rounded blob. Pass cornerRadiusTop AND cornerRadiusBottom.
authoringRecipe.bumpIntensity: 0.8-2. At 3+ hard texture bands throw specular highlights and rock reads as crumpled foil.
authoringRecipe.dustIsNormalBased: the dust layer settles by surface normal, not altitude, so on a cone it covers everything. For a snow line use a separate cap mesh, not coverage.
authoringRecipe.planarProjectionIsWorldScale: planar/triplanar map in world units, so on small props one tile spans more than the face. Cube faces take projection:'uv' cleanly.
authoringRecipe.glassNeedsContrast: transmission over a dark background reads black. Keep attenuationDistance near the object's size (~11 for a 15 m shard); 60 bleaches it colourless.
authoringRecipe.repeatMustBeHigh: triplanar/planar map in WORLD units, so a low repeat shows one flat fraction of the tile on a small prop. Use repeat 18-26 for 10-25 m objects, 30-40 for sub-5 m parts. This was why the wreck and civic block first read as untextured slabs.
authoringRecipe.textureDominatesBaseColor: at texture alpha ~0.9 the tile's own tone controls the look — darkening color() barely shows. Redraw the tile to change value.
authoringRecipe.torusIgnoresParams: mesh('Torus',{radius,tube}) ignores both — every torus spawns ~100 units across. Scale it, or use another primitive.
authoringRecipe.scaleMultiplies: scale({...}) MULTIPLIES the current scale rather than setting it. Repeated calls compound (0.85*0.9*0.88=0.67). Set it once.
authoringRecipe.groupingRebasesChildren: after group(), child position() values are LOCAL to the group origin, not world. Absolute values applied post-grouping shift parts badly — the geyser plume floated ~11 m off its vent this way. Read local positions back before repositioning children.
authoringRecipe.reservedHelperNames: the DSL already defines rock(); a local function of the same name is shadowed and throws. Prefix helpers (mkRock).
authoringRecipe.glassIsBackgroundDependent: a transmission/glass layer refracts whatever is BEHIND it, so on a dark backdrop ice/crystal renders near-black. For library assets viewed against unknown backgrounds prefer color + opacity + fresnel + depth; reserve glass for cases where you also control the backdrop.
authoringRecipe.paintNeedsLowTextureAlpha: for painted surfaces keep the texture layer alpha ~0.45 so the base color reads; use the bump map for the corrugation instead of tone. At alpha 0.72 every container rendered grey regardless of its paint color.
authoringRecipe.generatedMeshOrientation: a generated mesh's CHILD already carries the upright rotation (r=90). Rotating the parent Empty as well double-rotates it and lays the model on its side. Read the child's rotation before touching the parent.
authoringRecipe.generatedMeshScale: reported size is the UNSCALED content bounds; world size = bounds * scale. Divide target metres by the largest bound to get the factor.

knownBlocker: The Spline MCP bridge is unreliable in two distinct ways. (1) Document targeting: create_file sometimes returns a previously-used document; gate every build by reading the scene first and requiring 1 object + the default #262626 background. (2) The private SCREENSHOT camera can render a DIFFERENT document than run_code is writing to — a relay edit was verified against the city dome's viewport. When a capture looks wrong, confirm with get_scene before 'fixing' anything; get_scene reflects where run_code actually is. (3) Generation jobs are tab-bound: get_generation reports 'unknown job' if the tab changes mid-run, but the mesh may still land in the scene — check before assuming the credit was lost.

authoringMethods.ai_generated: generate_3d_model(prompt) -> mesh with BAKED generated textures. Highest quality; costs credits. Mesh lands with arbitrary facing/scale/pivot and must be measured and scaled.
authoringMethods.ai_texture: layer('texture',{style:'prompt'}) -> AI-generated photographic texture on geometry you build. Async; renders a checkerboard until it resolves.
authoringMethods.hand_built: primitives + generateTexture canvas tiles. Free and instant, but produces flat single-material props. Lower tier.
